prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Aliases: Medication Order Gateway=Morrowglass; Pharmacy Technician=Copperfield; Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot=Cinderwake; Pharmacy Verification Station=Juniper; Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler=Bluejay; Registered Nurse=Larkspur; Medication Return Kiosk=Tallowmere; Biomedical Engineer=Stonewake. Morrowglass validates/timestamps orders, retains rejections, produces Order Reconciliation Snapshot. Cinderwake reconciles orders/dispenses/cabinets using snapshot, preserving identifiers/context/authorization/timestamps/dispositions; excludes cancellations, honors corrections, reviews duplicates, conservatively retains partial remainders; holds disagreements/unresolved transactions. Copperfield authorizes replenishment only with clear queue. Clinical Pharmacist produces Dose Exception Review Slip; documented authorization precedes release; inconclusive reviews remain held. Serious/time-critical exceptions escalate immediately; Medication Safety Officer reviews diversion/repeated-risk/harm. IT Operations Specialist receives Diversion Review Packet, investigates logs without changing clinical disposition. Stonewake assesses faults/return-to-service. Cinderwake stops affected picks, retains scans/quantities/holds, produces Priority Refill Tote Tag, presents packages to Juniper; Juniper verifies order/product/strength/quantity, blocks incomplete/mismatched verification, records evidence/reviewer/disposition, produces Batch Release Note. Copperfield checks packages/lot/expiry/cold-chain, produces Cold Chain Handoff Card. Hospital Courier records custody/produces Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record. Pneumatic Tube Network reconciles loads/destinations; manifest records packages/destinations/handling/assembly-time. East Tube Dispatch Console reports routes/status/sends Tube Route Exception Ticket; West Tube Dispatch Console controls authorized routing. Discrepancies hold; retries rechecked; faults require testing/authorization; alternatives require approved custody. Ward staff verify receipts; Larkspur checks refrigeration/locks. South Ward Cabinet Controller reports lock/access failures; both controllers record arrivals/destinations. North Ward Cabinet Controller uses tote tag/blocks holds; configuration defines locations/product-identifiers/thresholds/roles/limits, is versioned/reviewed/time-stamped/approved. Availability=confirmed inventory+movements; replenishment thresholds never override clinical restrictions. Require authenticated appropriate roles/additional high-risk confirmation; reject identity-mapping mismatch; missing current approved configuration blocks routine dispensing/reports investigation. Bluejay records compartment temperatures/probe/calibration/time, applies approved limits, alarms offline, retains local records; tracks medication/lot/expiry, access/user/time/stock/door-duration. Excursion/probe-loss stock stays

New part:
S183: East Tube Dispatch Console maintains the approved route map and the current availability status of supported pneumatic segments.
S184: East Tube Dispatch Console checks the selected route against the destination cabinet, current network availability, and approved routing configuration before releasing a capsule.
S185: The console confirms that the destination is reachable and that the route does not include a segment reported unavailable.
S186: Route selection uses the destination identifier and the latest approved configuration version rather than an operator-entered sequence of segments.
S187: Before dispatch, the console checks for conflicting capsule movements and confirms that required interlocks are satisfied.
S188: The Pneumatic Tube Network reports segment status, transfer progress, and delivery confirmation to the dispatch console.
S189: If route status is stale or incomplete, the console holds the capsule and displays the condition for operator review.
S190: A loss of communication with a route sensor prevents the console from treating the affected segment as available.
S191: An interruption during transit is recorded with the capsule identifier, last confirmed location, and time of the interruption.
S192: The console alerts a Pharmacy Technician when a transfer stops progressing or cannot be confirmed at its destination.
S193: After recovery, the console requires refreshed segment status and an approved route decision before dispatch resumes.
S194: Route and temperature records retain timestamps and equipment identifiers to support operational review and investigation.
S195: The Pharmacy Verification Station serves as the final controlled checkpoint before a medication is made available for dispensing.
S196: The Clinical Pharmacist compares the active medication order with the product, strength, dosage form, dose, route, and scheduled time.
S197: The Clinical Pharmacist also confirms that the patient identifiers and pharmacy label agree with the authorized order.
S198: The Pharmacy Technician checks package integrity, lot identification, and expiry before presenting the medication for verification.
S199: For designated high-risk medications, an independent second check is completed and recorded before authorization.
S200: Any mismatch places the medication on hold until the discrepancy is resolved by an authorized pharmacy professional.
S201: The verification record captures the approving staff identity, time, and medication identifiers for later review.
S202: The Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot remains inhibited from completing a dispense until the required pharmacy authorization is present.
S203: The Clinical Pharmacist resolves unclear or conflicting order details through the Medication Order Gateway before authorizing release.
S204: The South Ward Cabinet Controller receives the release note and applies its own approved cabinet configuration before enabling any compartment.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
